label: <DEL> delimiter step in long (L>=8) sequences
explanation: Mostly fires at the <DEL> step (77% of activation mass; about 9% of all delimiter steps), and much more often when the sequence is long: t=8/9 (L=8/9) carry about 77% of the mass. The predicate is precise only to about 24%. Most long-sequence delimiters do not fire, and which ones do depends on content that a few tokens do not capture well. Firing is enriched when m/x/y/h/q or digits appear in the original (counting them gives a small F1 gain). Secondary weak firing (about 22% of mass) in the copy phase, mostly on the first one to three copy steps and on inputs k/w/n/z/s, plus occasional firing at the last step of L=9. It almost never fires in the original phase. The strongest activations are at <DEL> in L=8-9 sequences, often carrying over weakly to the next step (the first copy output).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the third original token (most: x, m, 1, q, 0, k; least: b, p, r, j) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: g, r, z, b; copy phase: n, g, 0, o; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=2, L=4 & t=3.
